  \caption{Native end-to-end proofs of $N$ multiplications $x \cdot y = z$ of random $128$-bit integers ($z$ a $256$-bit integer): \ftwoz\ (Spartan over a transcript-sampled prime with the \ftwoz\ opening, $\lambda = 100$) and Binius64 (native multiplication, ring switching and BaseFold at rate $1/2$ with $241$ queries and rate $1/8$ with $121$ queries for $100$ bits). \emph{Witgen} is the native witness generation; \emph{prover} is the complete prover call after witness generation, commitment included; \emph{verifier} is the complete verification.   \caption{Native end-to-end proofs of $N$ multiplications $x \cdot y = z$ of random $128$-bit integers ($z$ a $256$-bit integer): \ftwoz\ (integer R1CS, Lambda100; Ligerito rate $1/2$ is Johnson, custom:1:4, early Round-0 OOD; rate $1/8$ is Johnson, custom:3:4, early Round-0 OOD) and Binius64 (native multiplication, ring switching and BaseFold at rate $1/2$ with $241$ queries and rate $1/8$ with $121$ queries for $100$ bits). Native security targets are reported separately; these are not a uniform complete-protocol bound. \emph{Witgen} is the native witness generation; \emph{prover} is the complete prover call after witness generation, commitment included; \emph{verifier} is the complete verification; \emph{peak mem.} is the high-water resident set of a separate child process proving and verifying once ($1$\,GB $= 2^{30}$ bytes).
